text:
marta: Quick idea — instead of a full sidecar per-tenant for the v4 payload shape, what if we ship a small ingress normalizer shim at the VPC edge that can rewrite a handful of deprecated fields into the new envelope?
alex: Curious — do you mean a per-ingress proxy (shared) rather than per-service sidecar?
marta: Exactly. One shared L4/L7 layer close to customer ingress. Lightweight rewrite rules, opt-in header for canary.
raj: Pros: single place to patch inconsistencies, easier telemetry. Cons: edge becomes stateful wrt client cohorts. Any thoughts on complexity?
kelly: Edge changes make me nervous for perf and SLOs. Normalizer latency budget needs to be microseconds, not ms. How would we avoid head-of-line/backpressure?
sam-infra: We can implement it as an async fast-path: check header, do stateless map+rewrite, then forward. No blocking I/O. Written in Rust/Envoy filter would be ~sub-ms on p95.
alex: Also need per-tenant opt-out. Some enterprise tenants will want to manage their own transform or opt into runtime compatibility. Can we toggle by header and by tenant config?
marta: Plan: default off, enable via header X-RW-compat: v4-shim for staged tenants, and a tenant flag in control-plane for full rollout.
raj: What about schema drift where fields are removed entirely (not just renamed)? We might need best-effort fallback semantics — e.g., synthesize a minimal `messages` array if client sent `input` field.
kelly: That smells like behavioral compatibility; we should be explicit about it. If shim synthesizes, we must tag responses so downstream customers know data was filled by shim. Add header `X-RW-compat-info: synthesized=messages`
marta: Agreed. Observability: emit counters for rewrites, synthesized events, and tenant opt-in ratio. Also capture sample payloads for regression evals (sanitized).
sam-infra: Security: must scrub PII before storing samples. We'll pipe samples through redact pipeline. Also KMS-tag samples.
alex: Rollout strategy: 1) unit tests + small Envoy filter bench; 2) deploy to internal staging; 3) opt-in header canary with 5 tenants; 4) tenant-flag gradual rollout; 5) global enable with kill switch.
raj: Fallback policy — if shim throws parsers error or exceeds latency threshold, route traffic to runtime fallback (v3-compatible runtime node pool) and increment a telemetry tag `compat.fallback=1`.
kelly: How do we handle streaming responses? Rewrites are easy for request envelope, but streaming chunk framing might differ between v3/v4. Edge needs to detect streaming protocol and avoid rewrapping mid-stream.
marta: Proposed approach: for streaming, only do request-side normalization pre-stream. Downstream runtime must still handle v3 frame compatibility. We'll gate streaming normalization behind a strict test harness.
alex: Can we add an automated regression alert — if normalized requests have >0.5% model-output-drop (measured by eval set) then auto-disable for that tenant?
raj: Yes, add evaluation hook into Optimize infra. If a rollback triggers, routing will flip to dedicated v3 pool.
deploy-bot: canary deployed filter to staging (envoy-filter/compat-normalizer v0.1) :rocket:
marta: Next steps: draft short RFC with the state machine (enabled/disabled/fallback), error codes, telemetry keys, and a minimal YANG-ish rule DSL for rewrites. I'll write the RFC and tag infra + runtime for signoff.
alex: Awesome. Add a small perf SLA in RFC: p50 < 200us, p95 < 800us for normalizer path. Otherwise baseline route.
kelly: Also include a runbook for detecting silent degradation (trend in `compat.synthesized` vs model-quality).
raj: Cool — I can pair on the RFC tomorrow morning.
marta: Thanks all, filing RFC today.
